name: Sicilian Najdorf
plans_white: The most ambitious tries are the English Attack (Be3, f3, Qd2, O-O-O followed by g4/h4) and the 6.Bg5 Main Line aiming at a kingside pawn storm. 6.Be2 is the positional approach: castle short, restrain ...e5 with f3, and play for c4. The Fischer-Sozin (6.Bc4) eyes f7 and works well with 0-0 and f4.
plans_black: Black's structure is the Najdorf hedgehog or Scheveningen-type: ...e5 cedes d5 but grabs space; ...e6 keeps the structure flexible. The key pawn break is ...b5 (sometimes ...d5 to free the position). On opposite-side castling, Black races with ...b5, ...Nbd7, ...Rb8/Rc8.
traps: Poisoned Pawn (7.f4 Qb6 8.Qd2 Qxb2)
Polugaevsky Variation 7...b5 sacrifices

name: Sicilian Sveshnikov
plans_white: White exploits the d5 hole with Nd5 maneuvers and tries to nail down the d5 outpost. Standard plan: Nd5, Bxf6 trading dark-squared bishops, then play on the queenside with c4 and a4-a5.
plans_black: Black plays for ...Bg7 setups, ...f5 breaks, and uses the strong dark-squared bishop. Accepts structural weakness (d5/d6) in return for active piece play and the bishop pair.
traps: Sveshnikov main line 11.Bxf6 gxf6 with double-edged play

name: Sicilian Dragon
plans_white: Yugoslav Attack (Be3, f3, Qd2, O-O-O, h4-h5) is the main test: race Black's king down with a pawn storm. The Bxh6 sacrifice followed by h5xg6 is a thematic breakthrough.
plans_black: Black's fianchettoed bishop on g7 is the dragon's tooth. Standard race plan: ...Nc6, ...Bd7, ...Rc8, ...Ne5, then ...Rxc3 exchange sacrifice to shatter White's queenside. Also ...a6/...b5 expansion.
traps: Soltis 9.O-O-O d5 immediate counter
Rxc3 sacrifices to expose White king

name: Sicilian Alapin (c3 Sicilian)
plans_white: White prepares d4 to set up a Maroczy/IQP structure. Develops Nf3, Bd3, O-O. The plan is to occupy the center and avoid Black's prepared Sicilian theory.
plans_black: Two main replies: 2...d5 (most direct, equalizing classical center play) or 2...Nf6 (provokes 3.e5 and play against the e5 pawn). Black aims for ...e6, ...d5, ...cxd4 with equal play.
traps: 2...d5 3.exd5 Qxd5 4.d4 cxd4? 5.cxd4 wins back the pawn with structure

name: Sicilian Rossolimo
plans_white: White avoids open Sicilian theory. The standard idea is Bxc6 doubling Black's pawns, then prepare d3/d4 with a positional grip. Often c3 and d4 break in classical setups.
plans_black: Two main responses: 3...g6 (modern, fianchetto) or 3...e6 (solid, prepares Nge7). After 3...g6, Black accepts doubled pawns for the bishop pair and dark-square play.
traps: 3...g6 4.Bxc6 bxc6 5.O-O Bg7 — standard structural plan

name: French Defense
plans_white: White can choose Advance (3.e5, claim space, attack kingside), Tarrasch (3.Nd2, flexible), Classical (3.Nc3, sharp main lines with Bg5), or Exchange (3.exd5, drawish).
plans_black: Black's two pawn breaks are ...c5 (challenges the d4 chain) and ...f6 (challenges e5). The light-squared bishop is a problem piece — often traded via ...Bd7-Ba4 or developed via ...b6 fianchetto.
traps: Winawer Poisoned Pawn (3.Nc3 Bb4 4.e5 c5 5.a3 Bxc3+ 6.bxc3 Ne7 7.Qg4 Qc7 8.Qxg7 Rg8 9.Qxh7 cxd4)

name: French Winawer
plans_white: After 4.e5 c5 5.a3 Bxc3+ 6.bxc3 Black has the bishop pair but White has the center and attacking chances on the kingside (Qg4, h4-h5). White aims to use the c1-h6 diagonal and break with f4-f5.
plans_black: Black plays ...Ne7, ...Qc7, ...b6, ...Ba6 trading the bad bishop, then queenside expansion with ...Nbc6 and pressure on c3. The bishop pair gives long-term chances.
traps: Poisoned Pawn 7.Qg4 Qc7 8.Qxg7 Rg8 9.Qxh7

name: French Advance
plans_white: White gains kingside space with e5 and Bd3, aims for f4-f5 break and direct kingside attack. Often supports e5 with Nf3 and c3.
plans_black: Black plays ...c5 hitting the chain, ...Nc6, ...Qb6 pressuring b2 and d4. The light-squared bishop comes out via ...Bd7-Ba4 to challenge the queenside.
traps: 6...Qb6 7.dxc5? Bxc5 with strong dark-square pressure

name: Caro-Kann Advance
plans_white: Modern handling: 4.Nf3 (avoids the strong ...Bf5 setups) or the sharp 4.h4 lunge (Tal Variation) preparing g4. Plan: kingside expansion or central c3-d4-Nb1-d2-f3-h3 structure.
plans_black: ...Bf5 develops the bishop outside the pawn chain (the key reason to play Caro over French). Plan: ...e6, ...c5 break, ...Nd7-e7-g6, solid play with the good bishop.
traps: 4.h4 h6 5.g4 Bd7 6.h5 with kingside cramp

name: Caro-Kann Classical
plans_white: Slight space advantage. Plan: Nf3, h4-h5 to harass the f5 bishop, Bd3, c4 break. Aim for a slight pull in the endgame.
plans_black: Black's structure is rock-solid. Plan: ...e6, ...Nd7, ...Ngf6, castle short, prepare ...c5 break. The Caro setup is famous for its endgame robustness.
traps: 10...e6 11.Bd2 Ngf6 with classical equality

name: Caro-Kann Panov-Botvinnik Attack
plans_white: Sharp central play with isolated queen's pawn structures. Develops Nc3, Nf3, Bd3, O-O. Plan: occupy e5 with a piece, kingside attack, e5/d5 breakthroughs.
plans_black: Block the IQP with ...Nf6, ...e6, ...Be7. Trade pieces and target the d-pawn. Counter-attack with ...Nb6 or ...b6 setups.
traps: 5...Nc6 6.Nf3 Bg4 7.cxd5 — pressure on c-file

name: Pirc Defense
plans_white: Three main systems: Austrian Attack (4.f4, ambitious central expansion), Classical (4.Nf3, solid development), 150 Attack (4.Be3 with Qd2/O-O-O/h4).
plans_black: Hypermodern: let White build the center, then attack it with ...c5, ...e5, ...Nbd7-c5. Aim for ...e5 break and active piece play. Kingside fianchetto gives long diagonal pressure.
traps: Austrian 4.f4 Bg7 5.Nf3 c5 6.Bb5+ Bd7 7.e5 — sharp central play

name: Scandinavian Defense
plans_white: After 2.exd5 Qxd5 3.Nc3, gain tempo on Black's queen and develop with Nf3, d4. Aim for kingside attack with Bc4, Qe2, O-O-O.
plans_black: 3...Qa5 (most popular, eyes c3) or 3...Qd6 (modern). Plan: ...c6 luft, ...Nf6, ...Bf5/...Bg4, ...e6, develop solidly. Avoid the trapped queen with ...c6 always.
traps: 3...Qa5 4.d4 Nf6 5.Nf3 c6 6.Bc4 Bf5 — Bf5 is essential before ...e6

name: Ruy Lopez (Spanish)
plans_white: The Spanish is the most positionally rich open game opening. After 3...a6 4.Ba4 the bishop retains pressure on the c6-knight. Standard plan: c3, d3 or d4, Nbd2-f1-g3 maneuver, kingside expansion or attack.
plans_black: Main lines: Closed Spanish (...Nf6, ...Be7, O-O, ...d6, ...Na5-c4, ...c5), Marshall Attack (...d5!? gambit), Berlin Defense (...Nf6 trading queens). The Closed Spanish gives rich positional chess; the Berlin a famous solid endgame.
traps: Marshall Attack 8...d5 9.exd5 Nxd5 10.Nxe5 Nxe5 11.Rxe5 c6 — gambit for activity

name: Ruy Lopez Berlin Defense
plans_white: After 4.O-O Nxe4 5.d4 Nd6 6.Bxc6 dxc6 7.dxe5 Nf5 8.Qxd8+ Kxd8, the famous Berlin endgame: White has structural superiority, Black has bishop pair and active pieces. Plan: open the position carefully, target the f5 knight.
plans_black: The Berlin Endgame: trade queens, accept the loss of castling, but reach a balanced endgame with the bishop pair and resilient structure. Activate pieces with ...Ke8, ...h6, ...Be7 development.
traps: Anti-Berlin 4.d3 — avoids the endgame, plays positional chess instead

name: Ruy Lopez Marshall Attack
plans_white: After accepting the pawn (11.exd5 Nxd5 12.Nxe5), the defensive task is concrete: return material if needed, consolidate, push the pawn. The Anti-Marshall (8.a4 or 8.h3) avoids the gambit entirely.
plans_black: Sacrifice a pawn for sustained kingside initiative. Standard line: ...Nxd5, ...Nxe5, ...c6, ...Bd6, ...Qh4, ...Bg4 with attacking pressure on h-file and kingside. Worth a pawn long-term.
traps: Anti-Marshall 8.a4 — most common at top level to avoid the prepared gambit

name: Italian Game
plans_white: Quiet Italian (Giuoco Pianissimo) with c3, d3, Nbd2, Re1 — modern top-level approach. Plan: slow buildup, Nf1-g3 maneuver, h3, kingside expansion. Or the Evans Gambit (4.b4) for sharp play.
plans_black: Mirror the white setup or play the Two Knights with ...Nf6. Classical Italian setup: ...Bc5, ...d6, ...O-O, ...a6, ...Ba7, ...h6 — symmetrical solidity.
traps: Légal's Mate via Bg5 + Nd4 in fast development
Fried Liver 4.Ng5 d5 5.exd5 Nxd5 6.Nxf7!?

name: Italian Game: Giuoco Piano
plans_white: Modern Giuoco Pianissimo: 4.c3, 5.d3, 6.O-O, slow buildup with Re1, Nbd2-f1-g3. Avoid early d4 push, prefer long maneuvering.
plans_black: Mirror plan: ...c6, ...d6, ...O-O, ...a6, ...Ba7, ...h6. Both sides build slowly toward kingside maneuvers.
traps: Old Main 4.c3 Nf6 5.d4 exd4 6.cxd4 Bb4+ 7.Nc3 Nxe4 — classical complications

name: Scotch Game
plans_white: After 3...exd4 4.Nxd4, open central play with rapid development. Mieses Variation (4...Nf6 5.Nxc6 bxc6 6.e5 Qe7 7.Qe2 Nd5 8.c4) for sharp middlegame.
plans_black: Most reliable: 4...Bc5 (Classical), 4...Nf6 (modern, leads to Mieses Variation), or 4...Qh4 (sharp). Aim for quick development and central play.
traps: Steinitz 4...Qh4 risks the queen, needs preparation

name: Petrov / Russian Defense
plans_white: Classical: 3.Nxe5 d6 4.Nf3 Nxe4 5.d4 — slight central pull. The Marshall (5.Nc3) leads to sharper play. Modern try: 3.d4 (Steinitz).
plans_black: Symmetrical defense. The Petrov has a drawish reputation at the top level but offers solid black play. Plan: develop pieces normally, accept moderate space disadvantage, target weakened white pawns.
traps: 3.Nxe5 Nxe4?? 4.Qe2 Nf6?? 5.Nc6+ winning the queen

name: Vienna Game
plans_white: Two main approaches: 2.Nc3 with f4 (Vienna Gambit, aggressive) or 2.Nc3 with Bc4 (slow play). The Mieses System (4.g3 then Bg2) is a modern interpretation.
plans_black: Easiest reply is 2...Nf6 attacking e4. Defenders include 2...Nc6 mirror or 2...Bc5 active development. Avoid 2...d5? 3.exd5 — losing structure.
traps: Mieses Variation 2...Nf6 3.g3 Bb4+ 4.Bd2 — solid development

name: King's Gambit
plans_white: Sacrifice the f-pawn for rapid development and open lines. Plan: Nf3, Bc4 (or g3), O-O, attack the king. Heavy theoretical preparation needed.
plans_black: Accepted (2...exf4) leads to sharp tactical play. Falkbeer Counter-Gambit (2...d5) is a modern approach. Classical defense 2...Bc5 declines safely.
traps: Muzio Gambit 4.Bc4 g4 5.O-O gxf3 6.Qxf3 — incredibly sharp

name: Queen's Gambit
plans_white: The QG isn't really a gambit — Black can't easily hold the pawn. Three main directions: Accepted (2...dxc4, fight for c4 outpost), Declined (2...e6, solid), Slav (2...c6, robust structure).
plans_black: Choose between QGA (fight for the c-pawn with ...a6 and ...b5), QGD (Orthodox with ...Nf6, ...Be7, ...O-O), or Slav (...c6 supporting d5, ...Bf5 development).
traps: QGA 3.e3? b5 4.a4 c6 — Black holds the pawn

name: Queen's Gambit Declined: Orthodox
plans_white: Standard Carlsbad structure: cxd5 exd5 leading to minority attack on the queenside (b4-b5). Or classical setup with Bg5, e3, Bd3, Qc2, O-O, and central play.
plans_black: Carlsbad structure offers ...c6 + ...Nbd7 setup with the minority attack defense. Plan: trade dark bishops, contest d5 outpost, defend queenside, look for ...e5 break.
traps: Cambridge Springs 5...c6 6.e3 Qa5 — pinning the c3 knight

name: Slav Defense
plans_white: Main lines: 3.Nf3 (most flexible), 3.cxd5 cxd5 (Exchange Slav, drawish), 3.Nc3 (preparing e4). Plan: classical development, queenside expansion, central breaks.
plans_black: Classical Slav: ...Nf6, ...dxc4, ...Bf5 (the key — develops the bishop outside the pawn chain). Semi-Slav alternative with ...e6 + ...c6 (Meran/Anti-Meran complex). The Slav avoids the French problem of the bad bishop.
traps: Marshall Gambit 4.Nc3 dxc4 5.a4 — locks Black in

name: Semi-Slav Defense
plans_white: Anti-Meran (5.Bg5) leads to Moscow/Botvinnik variations — extremely sharp. The Anti-Moscow (5.Bg5 h6 6.Bxf6) gives White good chances.
plans_black: Meran (6.Bd3 dxc4 7.Bxc4 b5) — solid pawn break with ...c5. Or play the sharper Botvinnik (5.Bg5 dxc4 6.e4 b5 7.e5 h6 8.Bh4 g5 9.Nxg5 hxg5 10.Bxg5 Nbd7 — incredibly complex.
traps: Botvinnik System: pawn structure leads to wild tactics

name: Catalan Opening
plans_white: g3 + Bg2 — the Catalan bishop is the soul of the opening. Plan: develop Bg2, O-O, Qc2, Nbd2-e4 or Rd1, occupy central files. Long-term pressure on Black's queenside.
plans_black: Open Catalan (4...dxc4 5.Bg2 a6) accepts material temporarily, holds with ...b5. Closed Catalan (4...Be7 5.Bg2 O-O 6.O-O dxc4 7.Qc2) is solid. Avoid passive play.
traps: Open Catalan 4...dxc4 5.Nf3 Bb4+? 6.Nc3 c5? — concrete problems

name: London System
plans_white: London setup with Bf4, e3, Nbd2, c3, Bd3, O-O. Modern Nimzo-London plays for Ne5, h4-h5, kingside attack. Solid, low-theory opening for ambitious White players.
plans_black: Easiest counter is ...c5 + ...Nc6 + ...Bf5 (mirror the London). Or ...g6 setups against the London (King's Indian-like). Avoid passive play.
traps: 3.Bf4 c5 4.e3 Nc6 5.Nbd2 Qb6 — pressuring b2 immediately

name: King's Indian Defense
plans_white: Main systems: Classical (4.e4 d6 5.Nf3 — quiet), Sämisch (4.e4 d6 5.f3 — solid), Fianchetto (4.Nf3 + g3 — drawish), Four Pawns (4.e4 d6 5.f4 — aggressive but unsound), Averbakh (5.Be2 + Bg5).
plans_black: Hypermodern setup: ...Bg7, ...d6, ...O-O, ...Nbd7 or ...Nc6, then ...e5 break or ...c5 break. Famous race: White attacks queenside (c5 break), Black attacks kingside (f5 break, ...Nf6-h5, ...g5-g4).
traps: Classical Mar del Plata 9...Ne8 10.c5 f5 — racing attacks

name: Grünfeld Defense
plans_white: Exchange Variation (4.cxd5 Nxd5 5.e4 — most popular): build huge center, Black attacks it. Russian (4.Qb3) puts pressure on d5. Bg5 systems (4.Bg5) try to disrupt.
plans_black: Exchange: ...Nxc3, ...Bg7, ...c5 challenging the center, ...Nc6, ...Bg4 pin. The whole point is to attack White's center later. Dynamic Hypermodernism at its finest.
traps: Exchange 7...c5 8.Be3 Qa5 with strong central pressure

name: Nimzo-Indian Defense
plans_white: Three main systems: Rubinstein (4.e3 — flexible), Classical (4.Qc2 — recapture on c3), Sämisch (4.a3 — force the trade, accept doubled c-pawns for bishop pair).
plans_black: Block White's structure with ...d5/...c5, trade the bishop on c3 to give White doubled pawns, target the c4 and c3 pawns. Activate the light-squared bishop via ...b6/...Ba6.
traps: Classical 4.Qc2 d5 5.cxd5 exd5 — gives Carlsbad-like structure with extra c-file pressure

name: Queen's Indian Defense
plans_white: Petrosian Variation (4.a3) — prepares Nc3 without ...Bb4 pin. Classical (4.g3) — match the fianchetto. Both aim for c5 break or central majority.
plans_black: ...Bb7 fianchettoes the light-squared bishop, applies pressure on the long diagonal and e4. Plan: ...Be7, ...O-O, ...d5/...d6 setup, ...Ne4 jump.
traps: Petrosian 4.a3 Bb7 5.Nc3 d5 — fights for d5

name: Benko Gambit
plans_white: Accept (4.cxb5) leads to standard Benko positions. Decline (4.Nf3 or 4.Qc2) avoids the gambit. After accepting, defend the extra pawn with patience: e3, Be2, O-O, develop slowly.
plans_black: Long-term positional sacrifice. Plan: open a-file and b-file with ...a6 ...axb5, fianchetto with ...g6, ...Bg7, ...O-O, ...Ra7-c7 batteries, ...Qa5/...Qa8. Sustained queenside pressure for the pawn.
traps: Modern accepted line 4.cxb5 a6 5.bxa6 g6 6.Nc3 Bxa6 — typical Benko activity

name: Dutch Defense
plans_white: Anti-Dutch tries: 2.Bg5 (Hopton — annoying pin), 2.Nc3 (preparing e4), 2.g3 (fianchetto matching). Standard plan: develop classically, prepare e4 break or fianchetto setup.
plans_black: Three main systems: Stonewall (...d5, ...e6, ...c6, ...Bd6 — solid but locks the c8 bishop), Classical (...d6, ...e6, ...Nf6 — flexible), Leningrad (...g6, ...Bg7 — King's Indian-like with active kingside).
traps: Anti-Dutch 2.Bg5 — surprisingly effective at club level

name: English Opening
plans_white: Hyper-flexible opening. Main systems: Reversed Sicilian (after 1...e5), Symmetrical English (after 1...c5), Anglo-Indian (after 1...Nf6). Often transposes to Nimzo, Catalan, or King's English structures.
plans_black: Choose based on the rest of the opening: 1...e5 (Reversed Sicilian — sharp), 1...Nf6 (most flexible — wait for White's commitment), 1...c5 (symmetrical — solid), 1...e6 (queen's pawn-like).
traps: Symmetrical English 1...c5 2.Nc3 g6 3.g3 Bg7 4.Bg2 Nf6 — classical setup for both

name: Réti Opening
plans_white: Hypermodern: control center from afar with Bg2, c4, b3+Bb2. Often transposes into English, Catalan, or KIA structures. Aim for slow positional play.
plans_black: Best to determine intent: 1...d5 (classical center) or 1...Nf6 (mirror flexibility). Avoid early commitments.
traps: Réti Gambit 1...d5 2.c4 — classical center vs hypermodern attack

name: Trompowsky Attack
plans_white: Provoke ...h6 to gain tempo or play Bxf6 to double Black's pawns. Modern handling: 3.Bxf6 exf6 with positional play, or 3.Bh4 keeping tension.
plans_black: Most natural: 2...e6 keeping flexibility. Or 2...Ne4 attacking the bishop. Avoid loss of tempo with ...h6.
traps: 2.Bg5 Ne4 3.Bf4 c5 — early counter-strike

name: Modern Defense
plans_white: Two main approaches: classical 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 d6 (transposes to Pirc) or 2.d4 Bg7 3.c4 (clamp setup). Aim for big center.
plans_black: Delayed Nf6 allows ...c5 breaks immediately. Plan: ...Bg7, ...d6, ...Nd7, ...e5 or ...c5 break. Hypermodern flexibility.
traps: 1...g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 c5! — early central strike

name: Nimzowitsch Defense
plans_white: Easiest reply: 2.d4 e5 3.d5 (push the pawn) leading to French-like positions. Or 2.Nf3 — transposes to standard openings if Black plays ...e5 or ...d6.
plans_black: Surprise weapon. After 2.d4 plan: ...d5 or ...e5 with hypermodern central pressure. Avoid passive play with knight stuck on c6.
traps: 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 dxe4 — equal material, free development

name: Alekhine's Defense
plans_white: Four Pawns Attack (4.f4 — risky but ambitious), Modern (4.Nf3 — solid), Exchange (4.exd5 — drawish). Aim for the big pawn center.
plans_black: Provoke White into overextending. Plan: ...Nf6-d5-b6, harass center pawns, ...c5/...e6 breaks. Plays for endgame against overextended pawn structure.
traps: Four Pawns 4.f4 — overextends, classical refutation with ...dxe5/...c5

name: Philidor Defense
plans_white: Easy plan: develop classically with Nf3, Bc4, d4 break. Aim for kingside attack. Black's position is cramped from the start.
plans_black: Hanham Variation 3...Nd7 4.Bc4 c6 keeps solid but passive position. Modern handling allows ...d5 break later.
traps: 3.Bc4 Nbd7?? 4.dxe5 Nxe5?? 5.Bxf7+ — classical opening trap

name: Ponziani Opening
plans_white: Aim for d4 with full backup. Avoid standard Italian/Spanish theory. Plan: d4, Nc3 setup, kingside development.
plans_black: Two main replies: 3...Nf6 (attacks e4) or 3...d5 (immediate counter-strike). Either provides easy equality.
traps: 3...Nf6 4.d4 Nxe4 — winning the e-pawn

name: Italian Game: Two Knights, Fried Liver
plans_white: After 5.Nxf7!? Kxf7, ride the king attack with Qf3+ winning back material. Strong at amateur level, less effective at master level (Black has solid defenses).
plans_black: Counter with 5...Na5 — kicking the bishop, Black sacrifices a pawn for development and attack. The Fritz Variation 5...Nd4!? is also viable.
traps: Main Fried Liver — Black king walks toward danger but defends concretely

name: Scotch Gambit
plans_white: Sacrifice the d-pawn for rapid development. Plan: Bc4 hitting f7, O-O, Nc3, target the kingside. Aim for early Ng5 attacking f7 or e5 breakthrough.
plans_black: Two main defenses: 4...Bc5 (active development) or 4...Nf6 (immediate counter). Accept the pawn or transpose to safer lines.
traps: Cochrane Gambit 5.O-O Bc5 — sharp tactical play

name: Closed Sicilian
plans_white: Avoid open Sicilian theory. Plan: g3, Bg2, d3, Nge2, O-O, then f4-f5 kingside expansion. Slow positional buildup.
plans_black: Mirror white: ...Nc6, ...g6, ...Bg7, ...d6, ...e6, then ...Nge7, ...O-O. Often plays ...Rb8 + ...b5 queenside counter.
traps: Standard plan: both sides develop fianchetto, race for first attack

name: Réti: KIA
plans_white: Plan: Bg2, O-O, d3, Nbd2, e4 (the key central break), Re1, prepare kingside attack with Nf1-h2-g4 or Bf4-h6.
plans_black: Best is classical with ...c5, ...Nc6, ...e6, ...Be7 mirroring White. Or play directly for ...e5 break.
traps: KIA vs French 1.e4 e6 2.d3 d5 3.Nd2 — comes from many move orders

name: Four Knights Game
plans_white: Most popular: Glek 4.g3 with fianchetto. Or Scotch Four Knights 4.d4 for sharp central play. Spanish Four Knights 4.Bb5 for positional play.
plans_black: Symmetrical: 4.Bb5 Bb4. Or break symmetry with 4.Bb5 Nd4 (Rubinstein). Aim for easy development and central equality.
traps: Halloween Gambit 4.Nxe5? Nxe5 5.d4 Nc6 6.d5 — sound or unsound? Reputation says unsound but tricky
